verdict: FIS's revenue jumped 27% to $3.5B because it bought Total Issuing Solutions — like-for-like growth was 3.7% — while interest costs on the deal debt held GAAP profit to $356M.

segments.name: Banking Solutions
segments.note: Technology for banks — up 41% as reported because the acquired Total Issuing Solutions business is now included; on a like-for-like (pro forma) basis it grew 3.9%.

segments.name: Capital Market Solutions
segments.note: Technology for capital-markets firms — recurring revenue grew 3.0%.

segments.name: Corporate and Other
segments.note: Non-strategic businesses being wound down or sold — down 22%.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: SG&A of $627M, partly offset by $8M of other operating income — shown net so the chart foots to reported operating income.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $199M — the cost of debt taken on to buy Total Issuing Solutions — plus $14M of other expense.
footerNote: Net profit in the chart is total net earnings of $357M; $356M was attributable to FIS shareholders and $1M to noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.title: Real growth is 3.7%, not 27%
takeaways.text: The 27% reported jump mostly reflects adding Total Issuing Solutions. On a pro-forma basis — as if FIS had owned it all along — revenue grew 3.7% and adjusted EBITDA 5.2%.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS vs $0.69 GAAP
takeaways.text: Adjusted net earnings were $831M ($1.61 a share) versus $356M GAAP ($0.69). The gap is mostly $320M of purchase-accounting amortization and $147M of acquisition and integration costs.

takeaways.title: Deleveraging comes first
takeaways.text: Debt stood at $20.8B after the acquisition. FIS has paused buybacks and tuck-in deals to pay debt down toward its ~2.8x leverage target, while keeping the dividend.

oneTimers: FIS closed the acquisition of Total Issuing Solutions (the former Global Payments issuer business) in 2026; prior-year figures do not include it, which is why reported growth rates look so large.
On October 20, 2026, FIS sold a non-core prepaid business for gross proceeds of over $100M as part of its strategic portfolio review.
